description: F-CORE-032, the check that did not come with the field: a partner could be linked to account 9999 in books whose chart stops at 8400. The operation succeeded, the link was stored as a list of strings on the aggregate, and nothing ever reported it — master data wrong for every reader of the books, not only for the screen that entered it. That is the same argument that pulled `name` and `kind` into the library in the first place; the account link was made updatable in that pass and its validation was not. An embedding refused it in its own route with the chart already in hand (its F-17), which is the wrong place for exactly the reason the earlier three were. Replacing semantics are unchanged: a valid list replaces the previous one whole, and an empty list clears it.

steps.comment: An account the chart carries links as before.
One it does not carry is refused at creation — 9999 was accepted and stored.
And on update, where the list replaces the previous one whole.
The refusal changes nothing: the partner still carries what it carried.
An empty list still clears the link — refusing the unknown must not forbid the known-empty.
